query: What are the common advantage attributes of airlines whose overall rating is high?

per_column.name: seat_comfort_and_spaciousness
per_column.rationale: Provides a categorised comfort axis useful for identifying advantage attributes of high-rated airlines. Partly overlaps with the existing 'Seat Comfort' numeric column, reducing novelty, but the extracted qualitative categories add some grouping leverage. Values track the source text well (e.g. 'uncomfortable' → excellent was actually rated positively elsewhere; the Manchester row rated 'excellent' despite 'uncomfortable seating' is a slight mismatch but overall sound).

per_column.name: aircraft_modernity_and_condition
per_column.rationale: A genuinely new axis not present in original columns, useful for comparing advantage attributes. However groundedness is weaker: several rows produced 'well_maintained' where the text says nothing about aircraft condition (e.g. the Phnom Penh, Manchester, and Frankfurt reviews contain no condition cues), asserting a specific where the source is silent rather than returning NULL.

per_column.name: ground_service_efficiency
per_column.rationale: Distinct axis (check-in/ground handling) not captured by existing service columns, useful for grouping. Appropriately returns Unknown/NULL for silent rows (Phnom Penh, Manchester, Frankfurt), and 'smooth_efficient_seamless' for the Changi check-in row is well warranted by the text.

per_column.name: value_for_money_perception
per_column.rationale: Nearly redundant with the existing 'Value For Money' column and heavily near-constant ('good_value' dominates ~87%), giving little analytical leverage. Also, most sample reviews do not discuss price/value at all, yet a confident 'good_value' is asserted, indicating unsupported inference on silent rows.

per_column.name: food_and_beverage_quality
per_column.rationale: Adds a categorised food-quality axis; overlaps somewhat with the original 'Food & Beverages' rating but the qualitative categories provide grouping value. Values are strongly grounded in the source text (plentiful high-quality food → excellent_and_varied, etc.).

judge.rationale: Most added columns give qualitative, groupable attribute axes relevant to identifying advantages of high-rated airlines, and several (ground_service, aircraft_condition) are genuinely new relative to the original numeric ratings. Weaknesses: value_for_money_perception is largely redundant with an existing column and near-constant, and both it and aircraft_modernity_and_condition over-assert specific positive values on rows whose text is silent, rather than returning NULL — a source-groundedness concern. Food and seat columns are well grounded.
